sourceNote: Reviewed all supplied events, E0–E1356. No qualifying unsupported slogan or explicit protection against criticism was established. The transcript contains transcription errors and speaker changes within events; U marks inseparably mixed substantive turns. contrasts.speaker: A
contrasts.quote: history tends to get written by the standpoint of the winners
contrasts.explanation: The familiar phrase introduces a possible preservation bias, followed by a reason: later theological diversity makes complete earlier uniformity doubtful. E826–863 explicitly describe selective survival as a hypothesis and a guess, rather than a device that defeats every contrary finding.

contrasts.speaker: B
contrasts.quote: they're not even the room but we are at the table with our Orthodox brothers and sisters
contrasts.explanation: The identity-laden metaphor summarizes previously offered comparisons: shared councils and doctrines, the papacy as a major difference, and Protestant doctrinal departures (E970–1084). B later acknowledges convergence with some Lutherans (E1238–1251). The broad comparison remains disputable, but the metaphor does not replace an absent reason.
